about.title: Personal Injury Help in Arcata, California
about.longDescription: Arcata is a small city with a lot of foot, bike, and car traffic moving through the same stretches of road every day, and that mix shows up in the numbers. In the most recent full year on record, Arcata saw 37 injury collisions, 40 people hurt, and 1 traffic death. Public collision records point to Samoa Boulevard, Alliance Road, 11th Street, and H Street as the corridors with the highest volume of reported crashes, and reports tend to cluster on Friday nights between midnight and 2 a.m. None of that means a road is unsafe by itself — it's just where crashes have been recorded. What it does mean is that if you're injured in one of these collisions, or in a fall, dog bite, or other accident anywhere in Arcata, you're not alone and you have options. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured people in Humboldt County with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened. Attorneys in this network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Reaching out costs you nothing and doesn't commit you to anything.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but if a government entity like the City of Arcata is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you share some blame for what happened, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless You Win
items.desc: Attorneys connected through this service work on contingency, meaning legal fees only come out of a settlement or award — never out of your pocket upfront.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in Arcata?
items.answer: In most personal injury cases in California, you have two years from the date of the accident to file a lawsuit. If your injury involved a government entity or public property, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you were partly responsible. Your total recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, rather than being denied outright.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Arcata?
items.answer: Public collision records show that Samoa Boulevard, Alliance Road, 11th Street, and H Street have the highest volume of reported injury collisions in the city, with reports tending to cluster on Friday nights between midnight and 2 a.m. These are simply counts of where collisions have been reported, not a judgment about any road's safety.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and it costs nothing to have your situation reviewed. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, so they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is not a law firm and does not provide legal advice. We simply help connect injured people in Humboldt County with independent attorneys who can evaluate their situation.
